general.header:nth-of-type(1)>p:nth-of-type(1): What new blocks run, where new tabs start, and what a selection does.
general.section:nth-of-type(1)>div:nth-of-type(1: What new blocks on this PC run, as a login shell. Empty runs your login shell (powershell.exe).
general.section:nth-of-type(2)>div:nth-of-type(1: What Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Shift+Enter and Ctrl+Shift+O start. Ctrl+Shift+` always opens a shell block, Ctrl+Shift+A an agent block.
Splits always start in the directory of the block they split.
Where new windows and sessions on this PC start, and new tabs with no directory to inherit; a remote host's tabs start in its own. Empty, or a folder that is gone, starts at home.
general.section:nth-of-type(3)>div:nth-of-type(1: Finishing a selection puts it on the clipboard.
general.section:nth-of-type(4)>div:nth-of-type(1: Links in terminal output and program views. Ctrl-click always opens one; with Click, a drag still selects and programs that use the mouse, such as vim and tmux, keep plain clicks.
Alt with the click opens the other one. File links always open in Tern.
general.section:nth-of-type(5)>div:nth-of-type(1: Dotfiles show in the Files pane (Ctrl+Shift+. there). .git and .DS_Store never do.
The filter (Ctrl+Shift+F in Files) also looks inside ignored folders such as node_modules.
A folder holding only one folder shows as one row: crates / tern / src.
Files follows the editor block you work in, except inside ignored folders.
A click on a file shows it over your blocks until you click elsewhere (else double-click or Space).
general.section:nth-of-type(6)>div:nth-of-type(1: File blocks save without Ctrl+S. Unsaved text survives quitting either way, and a file changed on disk is never saved over.
general.section:nth-of-type(7)>div:nth-of-type(1: Open in Tern on folders, and Tern under Open with for text, code, images, databases and notebooks. Off removes them.
general.section:nth-of-type(8)>div:nth-of-type(1: New builds come from build.stencil.so. Restart to Update installs one at once.

Check every hour, download new builds in the background and install them when you quit. Off, Tern checks only when you choose Check for Updates, and a downloaded build installs only when you choose Re
general.section:nth-of-type(9)>div:nth-of-type(1: Tern installs omp from build.stencil.so, keeps it up to date, puts it first on PATH in its terminals and links it where your shell finds it.

agents.header:nth-of-type(1)>p:nth-of-type(1): What agent blocks run and where they open, when agents notify you while Tern is in the background, and the ACP agents Tern opens in its own chat.
agents.section:nth-of-type(1)>div:nth-of-type(1: Where a new agent block goes. Replace takes the tab's only pane when it is a shell idle at its prompt, and splits otherwise.
agents.section:nth-of-type(2)>div:nth-of-type(1: While Tern is in the background, an agent waiting for you (blocked or asking) posts a system notification. Clicking it goes to the agent's pane.
While Tern is in the background, an agent finishing or failing its turn posts a system notification.

Typing claude, codex or copilot in a new Tern shell opens it in Tern's chat over ACP. `command claude` runs its own interface.
Claude's chat shows a summary of its reasoning as it works. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 in the environment turns thinking off.
agents.section:nth-of-type(4)>div:nth-of-type(1: Commands that speak ACP over stdio. Environment variables are set in settings.json.
agents.section:nth-of-type(5)>div:nth-of-type(1: Tools agents get in Tern's chat. Environment variables and headers are set in settings.json; ${VAR} reads the environment.

appearance.section:nth-of-type(2)>div:nth-of-type(1: Appearance
Light, dark, or following the system.
Font
The terminal grid's family, or several, most wanted first; empty uses Ioskeley Mono Term. Beside it, the size of the grid and of code in editors, diffs and chats (Ctrl+Shift+= and Ctrl+Shift+− change
Bold font
Bold text's family, or several, most wanted first; empty uses Font's Ioskeley Mono Term Medium.
Italic font
Italic text's family, or several, most wanted first; empty uses Font's Ioskeley Mono Term.
Bold italic font
Bold italic text's family, or several, most wanted first; empty uses Font's Ioskeley Mono Term Medium.
Font weight
The terminal grid's text weight; bold draws 300 heavier, at least 700.
Code font
Monospace text outside the grid: editors, blocks and labels. Empty: editors follow Font, the rest use the built-in Ioskeley Mono Term.
UI font
The interface's family, or several, most wanted first; empty uses the built-in Geist. Beside it, the size of the rest of the window: tabs, menus, blocks and settings.
Line height
Added to each terminal and code row: whole px (2, -1) or a percentage (20%), as Ghostty's adjust-cell-height.
Cell width
Added to each terminal column: whole px (1, -1) or a percentage (-7%), as Ghostty's adjust-cell-width. Letters keep their size.
Padding
Room between a terminal's text and its block's edges: across, then down, as Ghostty's window-padding-x and -y.
Snap text to pixels
Draws every letter on whole pixels, as most terminals do: sharper, crisper text, with spacing up to half a pixel uneven. Off places letters at quarter pixels.
Contrast correction
Relights program text that reads too faintly on its background, to WCAG AA.
Reduce motion
Stills animations, the effort fire and the running pulses; programs drop their own motion too.

File blocks take it while editing code, text and Markdown.

appearance.section:nth-of-type(6)>div:nth-of-type(1: How omp's conversation reads: Reader in a centered column, Spine as a timeline of steps, Console in omp's own terminal look.
Runs of tool calls and thoughts collapse under one "Worked · Read ×2 · 1 thought" row once the answer follows, in every chat style.
omp's thoughts stay open in full, in line with the answer, without the "Thought" row that folds them. The one in progress keeps its spinner and timer.
The line along the top of omp's composer that fills as the conversation uses its context window; a click on it shows what fills it. Off, the composer draws none.
omp's composer stays open in full when you move to another pane. Off, it folds to one row — the session's name, any unsent draft and the usage — giving its room to the conversation.

How omp's composer shows your draft. Markdown styles it as it will read, as Notion does: bold, code, links, headings, lists and quotes, their marks hidden until the caret reaches them. Plain text show
Annotated keeps headings at text size, bold with a dim # marker, as omp's terminal view does. Automatic follows the chat style: Sized in Reader, Annotated in Spine and Console.
How native surfaces show diffs. Split puts old and new side by side when the pane is wide enough.
Columns per tab in code and diffs.

terminal.header:nth-of-type(1)>p:nth-of-type(1): How programs and the shell's prompt draw, and the profile Tern is built with.
terminal.section:nth-of-type(1)>div:nth-of-type(1: Ease mouse-wheel steps in terminals, files, lists and canvases. Off, scrolling is immediate and terminals scroll by whole rows. Respects Reduce Motion; trackpads follow the fingers directly and progra
Stretch and spring back when scrolling past the edges of terminals, files, lists and canvases. Off, scrolling stops at the edge.
When terminals show their draggable scrollbar. Automatic shows it while scrolling or when the pointer nears the right edge.
How far the mouse wheel and trackpad scroll terminals, files, lists and canvases, against the system's own speed.

Lines each terminal keeps, compressed in memory in the session daemon and in this window; lowering it frees the oldest at once, Clear frees them all. Crash recovery saves each terminal's newest 2 MiB.
terminal.section:nth-of-type(2)>div:nth-of-type(1: Programs that speak the Tern Surface Protocol (omp) draw native views. Off, they draw in cells.
Show recognized commands (git, ls, cargo, docker…) as native views; the raw output stays one click away.
A command's longer output folds to its first and last lines once it finishes, and one command keeps this many lines or an eighth of the scrollback, whichever is more. Never: every line stays.
Show Tab completions in a native popover; the shell still decides what completes.

Select with Shift and the arrows or by dragging in omp's composer, then type over it, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C or Ctrl+A; Ctrl+Z undoes instead of suspending omp. Off, or in Vim mode, every key goes to the prog

advanced.section:nth-of-type(1)>div:nth-of-type(1: What draws Tern's windows. Automatic uses the graphics card and stops using one that stops responding. Applies after a restart.
The GPU and graphics API the window draws with.
Smooth edges on shapes, borders and strokes. Text keeps its own smoothing.
Shades every edge at several samples per pixel: finer curves and hairlines, more GPU work. Lowered to what the GPU supports.
Frames wait for the display's refresh. Off shows them at once and may tear.
Frames the GPU may prepare ahead of the display: fewer answer input sooner, more keep heavy animation smooth.
